newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian police raid huge drug laboratory.
newsitem.headline: Canadian police raid huge drug laboratory.

text.p: Canadian police said on Tuesday they raided one of the biggest illicit drug laboratories ever in North America, seizing LSD, other hallucinogens and unfinished drugs worth nearly $42 million.

Five men and two women from Canada, the United States and Britain were arrested in the operation near Vancouver on charges of conspiring to manufacture and distribute narcotics, said Royal Canadian Mounted Police Sgt. Ken Ross.
Police conducted the raid on the laboratory in Port Coquitlam outside Vancouver last Thursday but did not announce the operation until Tuesday.
Police said they seized $4.6 million worth of drugs including LSD, the designer drug ecstasy and other hallucinogens bound for Europe, Canada and the United States.
Agents also found drugs in an intermediate stage of production potentially worth about $37 million, Ross said.

Police said the sophisticated drug-manufacturing operation may be the largest ever uncovered in North America. "This lab was next to none. Experts in this field are telling us they have never encountered one of this size before," Ross said.

For example police uncovered reaction flasks to make drugs that were six feet (two meters) high capable of holding 25 gallons (100 liters) of chemicals. "Normally the average reaction flask is about the size of tea kettle," said Ross.
Police also recovered nearly $520,000 in cash and gold along with rifles and handguns in the raid, Ross said.
